cases.prompt: We have an Order table with 40 columns and order_lines. OrderService loads the order with all lines eagerly, then updates the order and inserts a line. Should Order and OrderLine be separate aggregates?
expectations: States that OrderLine has no identity outside its parent, so it belongs inside the Order aggregate boundary
Explains that the boundary follows the rules that must hold in one commit, not the table count
Says the eager load plus line insert in one transaction is consistent with a single aggregate
Warns that a second aggregate in the same commit is a deliberate exception that must be documented
Recommends moving the line rules into the aggregate and keeping the service to a single load and save

cases.prompt: All our entities are @Entity classes with getters and setters. All logic is in OrderService which has 900 lines of if statements. Where do we start?
expectations: Names the model as anemic and explains the cause is that every rule was placed in the service
Gives the placement rule: a rule goes where the data it needs lives, so status rules move into the aggregate
Recommends removing setters and replacing them with intent-named methods that enforce the invariant
Says a domain service is only justified when a rule needs two aggregates or shared policy
Warns against moving every method at once, proposing one aggregate and one rule as the first slice

cases.prompt: Should Money, Email and OrderLine be @Entity classes in Hibernate, or something else? We store them in columns.
expectations: States Money, Email and OrderLine are value objects because they have no identity independent of their fields
Recommends records or plain final classes with value equality, not @Entity
Says the persistence mapping belongs in an adapter row or an @Embeddable, not in the value object itself
Explains the practical payoff: two logically identical values compare equal and can live in a Set
Warns against adding a surrogate id to a value object, which would silently change it into an entity

cases.prompt: We need Billing to know when an order is placed. Currently OrderService calls billingClient directly inside @Transactional. Should we use ApplicationEventPublisher?
expectations: Defines a domain event record such as OrderPlaced with past tense and only values the publisher controls
Publishes from the application layer, not from the domain, and notes the domain must not depend on Spring
Warns that an in-process event is not durable and that a listener failure inside the transaction rolls back the write
Recommends an outbox table when the publish must be atomic with the write, with consumers keyed for idempotency
Assigns retry and dead letter mechanics to the platform skill while keeping the modelling decision here

cases.prompt: Sales and Billing both have an Order class and they disagree about what status means. Support wants one shared Order entity. What do you recommend?
expectations: Identifies Sales and Billing as separate bounded contexts with different ubiquitous language
Rejects the shared entity, since one model cannot hold two sets of invariants
Recommends two models with a translation at the boundary, exposing a named interface or event contract
Notes a shared kernel is the most coupling-heavy option and only justified by a genuinely identical model
Explains each context keeps its own status enum and its own invariants, tested independently

cases.prompt: Internal admin tool, 6 tables, one writer per table, no rules beyond required columns and a status field we flip in two places. Should we build aggregates?
expectations: Recommends against full aggregate modelling for this case and gives the reason that there is no invariant to protect
Says a service plus a repository and a status enum transition is enough
Points out that the one rule worth protecting, legal status transitions, can live in the enum
Names the trigger that would change the answer, such as a cross-field rule or several writers of the same row
Warns against modelling a domain for use cases that do not exist yet
